title: Night Don Fall
tagline: The last danfo has dropped you. Your house is twenty minutes away, and the boys are somewhere ahead.

bonus.label: Keep your phone and money
bonus.lostMessage: You lost your money or your phone, so the bonus is gone.
bonus.earnedLine: You kept your phone and your money.

cash_low.label: No money left
cash_low.tip: You can't pay your way again.

dropped_name.label: You used a big name
dropped_name.tip: Lie gets easier, until somebody checks.

keke_ally.label: The keke man has your back

text.default: 10:40pm. The danfo conductor shouts “Last stop!” and everybody climbs down. Street lights are off, again. Your house is twenty minutes away on foot, and you and {rival} are both walking home: whoever gets to the gate first tells the story first. A last keke is idling at the junction. The main road is dark but empty. Past the bridge, the boys sit on the railings every night. Everybody knows.
text.coop: 10:40pm. The danfo conductor shouts “Last stop!” and everybody climbs down. Street lights are off, again. Your house is twenty minutes away on foot, and you and {partner} are walking home together. A last keke is idling at the junction. The main road is dark but empty. Past the bridge, the boys sit on the railings every night. Everybody knows.
text.solo: 10:40pm. The danfo conductor shouts “Last stop!” and everybody climbs down. Street lights are off, again. Your house is twenty minutes away on foot. A last keke is idling at the junction. The main road is dark but empty. Past the bridge, the boys sit on the railings every night. Everybody knows.

stakes.default: Choose how you walk home. Whatever goes wrong now follows you down the road.
stakes.coop: Stay close and stay smart. Whatever goes wrong now follows you down the road.

choices.label: Sweet-talk the last keke rider into one more trip
Walk fast down the main road, head down, no stopping
Start a loud phone call: “Yes Daddy, I dey close, come out with the boys!”
Take the inner street where people are still outside

recap.default: {winner} sweet-talks the keke rider until he sighs, “Last one o. Enter.” {loser} climbs in at the back, phone torch burning until the battery gives up.
recap.coop: You sweet-talk the keke rider until he sighs, “Last one o. Enter.”

recap.default: {winner} walks the main road fast, head down, eyes ahead. The dark does not bother anybody who keeps moving. {loser} is a full lamppost behind, breathing loud.
recap.coop: You walk the main road fast, head down, eyes ahead. The dark does not bother anybody who keeps moving.

recap.default: {winner} shouts into the phone, “Yes Daddy, I dey close, come out with the boys!” Three guys by a pole stop talking. {loser} tries to look like somebody's son too, and doesn't.
recap.coop: You shout into the phone, “Yes Daddy, I dey close, come out with the boys!” Three guys by a pole stop talking.

recap.default: {winner} turns into the inner street where generators are humming and people are still outside. {loser} follows, a little late and a little lost.
recap.coop: You turn into the inner street where generators are humming and people are still outside.

recap.default: {winner} tries to sweet-talk the keke rider, but he lifts his head, says “I don tire for tonight,” and drives off.
recap.coop: You try to sweet-talk the keke rider, but he lifts his head, says “I don tire for tonight,” and drives off.

recap.default: {winner} starts down the main road too fast, steps on a loose gutter slab, and the phone flies out of their hand. The torch dies on the tarmac.
recap.coop: You start down the main road too fast, step on a loose gutter slab, and the phone flies out of your hand. The torch dies on the tarmac.

recap.default: {winner} shouts “Yes Daddy, come out with the boys!” into a phone that isn't connected, and a voice by the pole laughs, “Which Daddy?”
recap.coop: You shout “Yes Daddy, come out with the boys!” into a phone that isn't connected, and a voice by the pole laughs, “Which Daddy?”

recap.default: {winner} takes the inner street and walks straight into a burial canopy across the whole road: chairs, speakers, one very serious bouncer.
recap.coop: You take the inner street and walk straight into a burial canopy across the whole road: chairs, speakers, one very serious bouncer.

tie.recap: Neither of you commits, and the keke rider drives off while you argue. A woman roasting corn calls you into the inner street.

keke_ride.title: Last Trip
keke_ride.text: The keke bounces through potholes on one headlight. The rider hums Fuji and does not say a word until the bridge shows up in the dark. He slows down. “This na where my road end,” he says. “After this one, na boys territory. I no dey go.” He isn't asking. Ahead, the bridge railings have little red dots on them: cigarettes.
keke_ride.stakes: He drops you here unless you give him a reason to go further.

choices.label: Ask him to keep his headlight on you until you cross. “Make dem see say person dey watch me.”
Pay ₦2,500 and ask him to carry you past the bridge

lock.reason: You don't have money left to pay with.

choices.label: Tell him your father is a DPO and he will hear about this
Agree to stop here, but ask which lane the boys don't use

recap.default: {winner} asks him to keep the headlight on them until the far side. He grumbles, then keeps it on. {loser} stands in the glare and is seen very clearly by everybody on the bridge.
recap.coop: You ask him to keep the headlight on you until the far side. He grumbles, then keeps it on.

recap.default: {winner} pays ₦2,500. He counts it twice, mutters, then guns the keke straight over the bridge and past the boys before they can stand up, and drops them at the vigilante post. {loser} watches the money go and the boys blur by.
recap.coop: You pay ₦2,500. He counts it twice, mutters, then guns the keke straight over the bridge and past the boys before they can stand up, and drops you at the vigilante post.

recap.default: {winner} says “My father is DPO.” His face tightens. He takes the bridge without a word, drops them at the next corner and does not say goodnight. {loser} sits stiff and hopes nobody checks.
recap.coop: You say “My father is DPO.” His face tightens. He takes the bridge without a word, drops you at the next corner and does not say goodnight.

recap.default: {winner} asks which lane the boys don't use. He points: “Behind the mechanic yard. Dark, but nobody dey there.” {loser} hears it too, and cannot unhear how dark it is.
recap.coop: You ask which lane the boys don't use. He points: “Behind the mechanic yard. Dark, but nobody dey there.”

recap.default: {winner} asks him to keep the light on. He yawns, kills the engine, and the headlight dies. On the bridge, four heads turn toward the sound.
recap.coop: You ask him to keep the light on. He yawns, kills the engine, and the headlight dies. On the bridge, four heads turn toward the sound.

recap.default: {winner} hands over ₦2,500. He takes it, stops at the bridge anyway, and says, “My own road end here.” He drives off with the money.
recap.coop: You hand over ₦2,500. He takes it, stops at the bridge anyway, and says, “My own road end here.” He drives off with the money.

recap.default: {winner} drops the DPO line. The rider laughs. “Every night, person be DPO pikin.” He puts them down right there, loudly, in front of the boys.
recap.coop: You drop the DPO line. The rider laughs. “Every night, person be DPO pikin.” He puts you down right there, loudly, in front of the boys.

recap.default: {winner} agrees to stop. He mumbles an answer, they miss half of it, and they walk into the wrong lane.
recap.coop: You agree to stop. He mumbles an answer, you miss half of it, and you walk into the wrong lane.

tie.recap: Nobody speaks. The rider shrugs and drops you at the foot of the bridge.

road_clear.title: Good Time
road_clear.text: You made good time. The street lamp is dead, but your eyes have adjusted, and the bridge is two hundred metres ahead. Four shapes on the railings. A cigarette glows. A small speaker plays Asake, low. Nobody has noticed you yet, which means you still get to decide how they meet you.
road_clear.stakes: You have about thirty seconds before they look up.

choices.label: Greet them like neighbours: “Boys! Una dey? Wetin dey?”
Pick up speed and cross before anybody can stand up
Hold your phone to your ear: “Yes, I'm at the bridge now, I see them”
Slow down, keep to the wall's shadow, and watch who is in charge

recap.default: {winner} greets them before they can greet them. One of them laughs and lifts his bottle. {loser} mumbles something half a beat late.
recap.coop: You greet them before they can greet you. One of them laughs and lifts his bottle.

recap.default: {winner} crosses the bridge at a near-jog, shoulders tight. By the time anyone stands, they are on the far side and the lights of the vigilante post are in sight. {loser} is not so quick and gets a long look.
recap.coop: You cross the bridge at a near-jog, shoulders tight. By the time anyone stands, you are on the far side and the lights of the vigilante post are in sight.

recap.default: {winner} talks into a phone nobody is on. The boys go quiet and look at one another. “Who be that one?” {loser} walks next to a very loud lie.
recap.coop: You talk into a phone nobody is on. The boys go quiet and look at one another. “Who be that one?”

recap.default: {winner} sees who matters: the one with the clean shoes, the one who is not drinking. They step back and turn into the lane behind the mechanic yard. {loser} follows, one step too slow, and brushes a boy's foot.
recap.coop: You see who matters: the one with the clean shoes, the one who is not drinking. You step back and turn into the lane behind the mechanic yard.

recap.default: {winner} calls out a greeting, but the voice comes out cheerful and wrong. The speaker clicks off. Four heads turn.
recap.coop: You call out a greeting, but the voice comes out cheerful and wrong. The speaker clicks off. Four heads turn.

recap.default: {winner} breaks into a jog, and the boys hear it. “Hey! Where you dey run go?” They are on their feet.
recap.coop: You break into a jog, and the boys hear it. “Hey! Where you dey run go?” They are on their feet.

recap.default: {winner} lifts the phone, the screen is dark, and somebody says, “Oga, your phone is off.” Everybody laughs, and then they stop laughing.
recap.coop: You lift the phone, the screen is dark, and somebody says, “Oga, your phone is off.” Everybody laughs, and then they stop laughing.

recap.default: {winner} stays in the shadow too long. A boy lights a cigarette and finds them with the flame. “Oga, why you dey hide?”
recap.coop: You stay in the shadow too long. A boy lights a cigarette and finds you with the flame. “Oga, why you dey hide?”

tie.recap: You hesitate. They notice. Ajala slides off the railing and walks over, slowly.

road_snag.title: Torch Don Die
road_snag.text: The phone is somewhere in the weeds, face-down, and the torch is gone. The clatter carried. Ahead, at the bridge, two shapes stand up from the railings. “Who dey there?” one calls. A third voice says, “Leave am, na just person.” You can hear them deciding how much they care.
road_snag.stakes: You can't see them, but they can hear you.

choices.label: Call back cheerfully: “Na me o! My phone just fall, I dey find am!”
Grab the phone by feel and keep moving, no explanation
Answer in a deep voice: “Na me. Who send you?”
Crouch, find the phone slowly, wait for them to lose interest

recap.default: {winner} calls back, cheerful and a little stupid. The boys laugh at the stupidity and relax. {loser} is laughed at too, for different reasons.
recap.coop: You call back, cheerful and a little stupid. The boys laugh at the stupidity and relax.

recap.default: {winner} finds the phone by touch, wipes the dirt off, and walks on before anyone can ask. It still will not light. {loser} pretends not to be rattled.
recap.coop: You find the phone by touch, wipe the dirt off, and walk on before anyone can ask. It still will not light.

recap.default: {winner} answers in a deeper voice than their own. A pause. “Eh, sorry sir,” one says, without meaning it. {loser} cannot decide between impressed and embarrassed.
recap.coop: You answer in a deeper voice than your own. A pause. “Eh, sorry sir,” one says, without meaning it.

recap.default: {winner} crouches, finds the phone, and wait. The shapes lose interest. They ease backwards into the lane behind the mechanic yard. {loser} follows on all fours.
recap.coop: You crouch, find the phone, and wait. The shapes lose interest. You ease backwards into the lane behind the mechanic yard.

recap.default: {winner} shouts a cheerful greeting into the dark, in the wrong direction. One of the boys is now very close to them.
recap.coop: You shout a cheerful greeting into the dark, in the wrong direction. One of the boys is now very close to you.

recap.default: {winner} grabs something in the weeds. It is a slipper, not a phone. By the time they stand, the boys are walking over.
recap.coop: You grab something in the weeds. It is a slipper, not a phone. By the time you stand, the boys are walking over.

recap.default: {winner} growls something tough. The voice cracks. The boys laugh, then come over to see who it is.
recap.coop: You growl something tough. The voice cracks. The boys laugh, then come over to see who it is.

recap.default: {winner} crawls around for the phone and ends up in the wrong lane, still in the dark, still without a torch.
recap.coop: You crawl around for the phone and end up in the wrong lane, still in the dark, still without a torch.

tie.recap: Nobody moves. After a while the boys decide you are not worth standing for. You walk on, blind, toward the bridge.

call_works.title: Daddy Is Coming
call_works.text: “Come out with the boys!” You can hear it travel down the road. By the pole, three guys stop talking. One steps back under the shop awning. Nobody says anything, which is better than anything. You have maybe two minutes before someone decides the call was fake. Ahead, the road splits: the bridge on the left, a lane behind the mechanic yard on the right. The phone is still pressed to your ear.
call_works.stakes: Your lie is working. It does not last.

choices.label: Walk past with a nod: “Chairman. Evening.” Like you belong
Keep talking into the phone and pick up speed
Raise the lie: “Tell Tee I'm passing, na him bridge”
End the call quietly and slip into the lane behind the mechanic yard

recap.default: {winner} nods at them like an old customer. The shortest one nods back before he can stop himself. {loser} hesitates, and the nod does not cover them.
recap.coop: You nod at them like an old customer. The shortest one nods back before he can stop himself.

recap.default: {winner} keeps talking and walks faster than anybody should walk and talk. Two blocks later, nobody has followed. {loser} is out of breath and out of lies.
recap.coop: You keep talking and walk faster than anybody should walk and talk. Two blocks later, nobody has followed.

recap.default: {winner} names “Tee” like they mean it. The boys exchange looks. There is, in fact, a Tee. Nobody likes this. {loser} would very much like to be anywhere else.
recap.coop: You name “Tee” like you mean it. The boys exchange looks. There is, in fact, a Tee. Nobody likes this.

recap.default: {winner} ends the call, steps off the road, and slides into the lane before the boys decide anything.
recap.coop: You end the call, step off the road, and slide into the lane before the boys decide anything.

recap.default: {winner} nods too late, and wrong. “You dey greet us like say we be your father?” someone says.
recap.coop: You nod too late, and wrong. “You dey greet us like say we be your father?” someone says.

recap.default: {winner} speeds up, which is exactly what people do when a call is fake. “Oga! Oga, wait.”
recap.coop: You speed up, which is exactly what people do when a call is fake. “Oga! Oga, wait.”

recap.default: {winner} says “Tell Tee I'm passing.” Silence. “Which Tee?” “Tee wey get bakery?” “No be that Tee.”
recap.coop: You say “Tell Tee I'm passing.” Silence. “Which Tee?” “Tee wey get bakery?” “No be that Tee.”

recap.default: {winner} steps into the lane and finds it blocked by a broken trailer. They have to come back onto the road, and the boys watch the whole thing.
recap.coop: You step into the lane and find it blocked by a broken trailer. You have to come back onto the road, and the boys watch the whole thing.

tie.recap: Neither of you commits. The boys at the pole stop being scared and start being curious, and you walk on to the bridge.

call_exposed.title: Which Daddy?
call_exposed.text: Laughter by the pole. A boy lifts his phone torch into your face. “Daddy? Which Daddy? Come, make we hear am.” Three of them stand up. They are not angry, they are bored, and that is worse. Behind them is the bridge. Ahead of you is the only road home.
call_exposed.stakes: Everybody heard the lie. Decide whether to own it.

choices.label: Laugh at yourself: “Oga, I lie small. Fear catch me.”
Turn and run for the lit street
Double down: “Na so I tell am, he don dey come”
Show them your screen, no call, and ask for the vigilante post

recap.default: {winner} owns the lie, smiling. The boys howl. “See this one!” It costs pride, not naira. {loser} stands there looking guilty, which entertains everyone.
recap.coop: You own the lie, smiling. The boys howl. “See this one!” It costs pride, not naira.

recap.default: {winner} turns and run, and the speed surprises them. By the time they decide to chase, the vigilante post's lamp is already ahead. {loser} gets a slipper thrown at them.
recap.coop: You turn and run, and the speed surprises them. By the time they decide to chase, the vigilante post's lamp is already ahead.

recap.default: {winner} holds the lie with a straight face. One boy pulls out his own phone, as if to check. The screen is cracked and blank. He puts it away. {loser} does not dare breathe.
recap.coop: You hold the lie with a straight face. One boy pulls out his own phone, as if to check. The screen is cracked and blank. He puts it away.

recap.default: {winner} shows the empty call log, apologises, and ask where the vigilante post is. They point, laughing, to the lit corner. {loser} has to hear about it the whole walk.
recap.coop: You show the empty call log, apologise, and ask where the vigilante post is. They point, laughing, to the lit corner.

recap.default: {winner} laughs. Nobody else does. “You think na joke?” The circle gets smaller.
recap.coop: You laugh. Nobody else does. “You think na joke?” The circle gets smaller.

recap.default: {winner} breaks into a run, a foot comes out of nowhere, and they hit the ground. The phone skids away. They are standing over them now.
recap.coop: You break into a run, a foot comes out of nowhere, and you hit the ground. The phone skids away. They are standing over you now.

recap.default: {winner} insists on Daddy. “Okay, Daddy, give us his number.” There is no number.
recap.coop: You insist on Daddy. “Okay, Daddy, give us his number.” There is no number.

recap.default: {winner} holds up the phone to prove it. “Oga, give am here, make we check.” They don't give it back quickly.
recap.coop: You hold up the phone to prove it. “Oga, give am here, make we check.” They don't give it back quickly.

tie.recap: Nobody speaks. After a long moment the boys sit back down, bored, and wave you towards the bridge.

corn_aunty.title: Mama Tolu's Corner
corn_aunty.text: The inner street smells of corn and kerosene. Mama Tolu turns cobs over the coals, three men play draughts under a bulb on a generator, kids are still shouting. It's slower than the main road, but you can see faces here. The street runs out near the vigilante post. Mama Tolu looks up. “Evening o. You dey go where this night?”
corn_aunty.stakes: People are around, so this is the safest part of the road. It will not last.

choices.label: Buy a cob, ask about her day, and say whose child you are
Offer ₦1,000 to her boy to walk you to the next corner

lock.reason: You don't have money left to pay with.

choices.label: Tell the draught men your brother is at the vigilante post, waiting
Ask which roads are blocked tonight and where the boys are

recap.default: {winner} buys a cob and chats until Mama Tolu says, “Tell Baba Sule at the post that Mama Tolu send you.” {loser} eats the cob in silence.
recap.coop: You buy a cob and chat until Mama Tolu says, “Tell Baba Sule at the post that Mama Tolu send you.”

recap.default: {winner} pays ₦1,000, and Mama Tolu's boy leads the way with a torch. He is twelve and knows every shortcut. {loser} sees the money go and the boy light up.
recap.coop: You pay ₦1,000, and Mama Tolu's boy leads the way with a torch. He is twelve and knows every shortcut.

recap.default: {winner} announces a brother at the vigilante post. A draught man lifts a brow. “Baba Sule nephew?” They nod. He goes back to his game. {loser} realises how thin that lie was.
recap.coop: You announce a brother at the vigilante post. A draught man lifts a brow. “Baba Sule nephew?” You nod. He goes back to his game.

recap.default: {winner} asks the right questions. Bridge has boys tonight, the back lane is worse, but the inner street runs clean to their own road. {loser} nods like they knew all along.
recap.coop: You ask the right questions. Bridge has boys tonight, the back lane is worse, but the inner street runs clean to your own road.

recap.default: {winner} tries to chat, but Mama Tolu is busy with three customers and looks right past them. They leave with no cob and no directions.
recap.coop: You try to chat, but Mama Tolu is busy with three customers and looks right past you. You leave with no cob and no directions.

recap.default: {winner} pays ₦1,000. The boy takes it, says “one minute,” and disappears behind a gate. He does not come back.
recap.coop: You pay ₦1,000. The boy takes it, says “one minute,” and disappears behind a gate. He does not come back.

recap.default: {winner} claims a brother at the post. “Which brother?” says the draught man. “Baba Sule has no brother here.” They leave faster than they came.
recap.coop: You claim a brother at the post. “Which brother?” says the draught man. “Baba Sule has no brother here.” You leave faster than you came.

recap.default: {winner} asks. Mama Tolu says the bridge is clear tonight. It is not.
recap.coop: You ask. Mama Tolu says the bridge is clear tonight. It is not.

tie.recap: Neither of you leads, so Mama Tolu points down the street herself, and tells you to keep to the lamps.

keke_gone.title: Dark Junction
keke_gone.text: The tail light shrinks to a dot and is gone. The generator across the road coughs once and dies. Now it is just the junction, the smell of burnt tyre, and your own breathing. A late okada slows beside you, and the rider kills his engine. “Where you dey go?”
keke_gone.stakes: You've lost time. Every road home is now a bit darker.

choices.label: Haggle with the okada rider, friendly and easy
Skip him and walk the main road fast
Pretend you're on the phone and walk like someone is picking you up
Take the inner street instead

recap.default: {winner} settles on ₦1,500, and the okada takes the bridge at speed. The boys on the rail look up, but the bike is already gone. {loser} holds the rider's shirt with both hands.
recap.coop: You settle on ₦1,500, and the okada takes the bridge at speed. The boys on the rail look up, but the bike is already gone.

recap.default: {winner} walks the main road fast. Without a torch, it's slower than it looks, and by the time the bridge appears, they are tired.
recap.coop: You walk the main road fast. Without a torch, it's slower than it looks, and by the time the bridge appears, you are tired.

recap.default: {winner} puts on a show. “Yes, I'm coming, I see the bridge.” The okada man chuckles and starts his engine, unconvinced. {loser} wonders why they are performing for a bike man.
recap.coop: You put on a show. “Yes, I'm coming, I see the bridge.” The okada man chuckles and starts his engine, unconvinced.

recap.default: {winner} takes the inner street, where the lights are, and comes out near the vigilante post with a clear head.
recap.coop: You take the inner street, where the lights are, and come out near the vigilante post with a clear head.

recap.default: {winner} loses the argument over the fare. The okada rider revs off, and they walk the rest to the bridge in the dark, in a bad mood.
recap.coop: You lose the argument over the fare. The okada rider revs off, and you walk the rest to the bridge in the dark, in a bad mood.

recap.default: {winner} hurries down the main road, trips, and curses out loud. The okada man pretends he did not see. The boys do not.
recap.coop: You hurry down the main road, trip, and curse out loud. The okada man pretends he did not see. The boys do not.

recap.default: {winner} plays the phone game badly. The okada rider laughs: “Another pikin wey get plan.” The laugh carries to the bridge.
recap.coop: You play the phone game badly. The okada rider laughs: “Another pikin wey get plan.” The laugh carries to the bridge.

recap.default: {winner} goes for the inner street. It's blocked. They double back through a narrow drain lane and lose ten minutes.
recap.coop: You go for the inner street. It's blocked. You double back through a narrow drain lane and lose ten minutes.

tie.recap: Nobody decides anything. The okada man shrugs and rides off, and you drift towards the bridge.

street_blocked.title: Burial Canopy
street_blocked.text: The inner street is shut: a big canopy, white plastic chairs, aunties in matching ankara, a DJ with speakers taller than the bouncer. It is half funeral, half owambe, and you can't be heard at normal volume. The bouncer has a black suit and a bad temper. The only ways out are through the party or down the drain lane behind the generator.
street_blocked.stakes: Nobody here can help you. Nobody here will notice either.

choices.label: Hug an uncle: “Sorry for your loss,” and ask to pass
Push through the crowd fast, shoulders low
Tell the bouncer you're the deceased's nephew
Take the drain lane behind the generator

recap.default: {winner} hugs the nearest uncle and says sorry. He sits them down with a plate of jollof, then walks them to the far end of the street. Turns out he is on the vigilante committee. {loser} gets one plastic spoon and a suspicious look.
recap.coop: You hug the nearest uncle and say sorry. He sits you down with a plate of jollof, then walks you to the far end of the street. Turns out he is on the vigilante committee.

recap.default: {winner} cuts through the crowd with shoulders low, dancing a little to look natural, and comes out the other side near the vigilante post. {loser} follows and steps on three people's shoes.
recap.coop: You cut through the crowd with shoulders low, dancing a little to look natural, and come out the other side near the vigilante post.

recap.default: {winner} claims to be the deceased's nephew. The bouncer's face loosens: “Condolences, sir.” The line parts. {loser} wonders what happens if somebody asks for the name.
recap.coop: You claim to be the deceased's nephew. The bouncer's face loosens: “Condolences, sir.” The line parts.

recap.default: {winner} slips behind the generator into the drain lane where nobody is looking.
recap.coop: You slip behind the generator into the drain lane where nobody is looking.

recap.default: {winner} hugs a stranger who is not impressed. The bouncer lifts them by the collar and puts them down in the drain lane.
recap.coop: You hug a stranger who is not impressed. The bouncer lifts you by the collar and puts you down in the drain lane.

recap.default: {winner} pushes in, and a hand slips into their pocket. By the time they shove out the other side, the phone is gone.
recap.coop: You push in, and a hand slips into your pocket. By the time you shove out the other side, the phone is gone.

recap.default: {winner} says “nephew.” “Which one?” says the bouncer. “Madam has no nephew.” They are shown out the back.
recap.coop: You say “nephew.” “Which one?” says the bouncer. “Madam has no nephew.” You are shown out the back.

recap.default: {winner} finds the drain lane, but it comes out right beside the bridge, in the light of the boys' speaker.
recap.coop: You find the drain lane, but it comes out right beside the bridge, in the light of the boys' speaker.

tie.recap: The bouncer looks at you both, shrugs, and points at the drain lane. You go.

bridge_toll.title: Toll
bridge_toll.text: Four boys on the bridge railings, bottles in hand. The leader, Ajala, comes down slowly, like a man who has all night. “Oga, good evening. Bridge no free. Una no know?” The others laugh, not unkindly. This is a toll. The only question is the price, and how it is paid.
bridge_toll.stakes: How you pay decides how you walk away.

choices.label: Laugh with them: “You boys wan make me poor before Christmas?”
Hand over ₦1,000 and ask them to open the way

lock.reason: You don't have money left to pay with.

choices.label: Say you're Tee's guy and they should check with him
Count them, find the sober one, speak only to him

twists.text: {holder}: Ajala squints. “I don see this face before. Na who you be?”
{holder}: One of the boys nods. “Na the one wey greet us.” The mood eases.
{holder}: Far behind, a keke headlight flashes once. Ajala notices.

recap.default: {winner} makes Ajala laugh. He waves the others off the railing. “Make that one pass. We go see am for Christmas.” {loser} slips through the gap with eyes on the ground.
recap.coop: You make Ajala laugh. He waves the others off the railing. “Make that one pass. We go see am for Christmas.”

recap.default: {winner} presses ₦1,000 into Ajala's hand. He counts it with his thumb, nods, and moves aside. Safe, but lighter. {loser} sees the money and the boys' faces.
recap.coop: You press ₦1,000 into Ajala's hand. He counts it with his thumb, nods, and moves aside. Safe, but lighter.

recap.default: {winner} drops Tee's name. Ajala's face changes. “Tee? Eh. Go, go.” They walk past quickly and do not look back. {loser} feels the cold of the lie at the back of the neck.
recap.coop: You drop Tee's name. Ajala's face changes. “Tee? Eh. Go, go.” You walk past quickly and do not look back.

recap.default: {winner} speaks only to the sober one. Ajala listens, shrugs, and lets them by. “Next time, greet properly.” {loser} says nothing and is glad.
recap.coop: You speak only to the sober one. Ajala listens, shrugs, and lets you by. “Next time, greet properly.”

recap.default: {winner} jokes and Ajala does not laugh. “You think say I dey play?” It costs ₦500 and a lot of dignity to cross.
recap.coop: You joke and Ajala does not laugh. “You think say I dey play?” It costs ₦500 and a lot of dignity to cross.

recap.default: {winner} hands over ₦1,000. Ajala says, “Phone too. Na toll plus service charge.” Two boys move closer.
recap.coop: You hand over ₦1,000. Ajala says, “Phone too. Na toll plus service charge.” Two boys move closer.

recap.default: {winner} names Tee. Ajala smiles a bit too nicely. “Tee is my brother.” Two of them peel off the railing and walk behind them “to see you off.”
recap.coop: You name Tee. Ajala smiles a bit too nicely. “Tee is my brother.” Two of them peel off the railing and walk behind you “to see you off.”

recap.default: {winner} picks the wrong boy. The drunk one is offended. It ends with ₦500 and an insult.
recap.coop: You pick the wrong boy. The drunk one is offended. It ends with ₦500 and an insult.

tie.recap: A long silence, then Ajala sighs. “Pass. Don't come back this way too soon.”

bridge_heated.title: Wetin You Dey Find?
bridge_heated.text: They are already off the railing. Four of them in a loose half-circle, and the nearest has a plank he does not pretend to hide. “Wetin you dey find for here this night?” Ajala does not shout. Shouting is for people who aren't sure. Somebody shifts behind you, between you and the road you came from. The bridge is thirty steps long.
bridge_heated.stakes: They are not asking for a toll anymore.

choices.label: Hands open, soft voice: “Chairman, I dey go house. My mama don dey wait.”
Bolt across the bridge and do not look back
Say the vigilante men are right behind you
Hand over ₦500 “for water” and ask politely for the road

lock.reason: You don't have money left to pay with.

twists.text: {holder}: Without a torch, you cannot read one face here. That frightens you more than the plank.
{holder}: Ajala: “Eh! No be you I see for the road before?”

recap.default: {winner} keeps their voice low and their hands open. Ajala studies for a while, then lets the half-circle break. “Go. Face front.” {loser} walks beside, cold sweat in the shirt.
recap.coop: You keep your voice low and your hands open. Ajala studies for a while, then lets the half-circle break. “Go. Face front.”

recap.default: {winner} runs. The first shout comes late and the second comes angry. By the time they clear the bridge, one pair of slippers is still slapping behind. {loser} is slower, and hears every slap.
recap.coop: You run. The first shout comes late and the second comes angry. By the time you clear the bridge, one pair of slippers is still slapping behind.

recap.default: {winner} says the vigilante men are behind. A pause. Ajala looks past them into the dark. “Hmm.” He steps back. They walk quickly toward the only light on the road: the real vigilante post. {loser} did not know there was a post, and is quietly thankful.
recap.coop: You say the vigilante men are behind. A pause. Ajala looks past you into the dark. “Hmm.” He steps back. You walk quickly toward the only light on the road: the real vigilante post.

recap.default: {winner} gives ₦500 “for water” and asks for the road. The half-circle breaks. {loser} says thank you to a plank.
recap.coop: You give ₦500 “for water” and ask for the road. The half-circle breaks.

recap.default: {winner} says “My mama don dey wait.” Somebody laughs. “Make we help your mama.” A hand closes on their phone.
recap.coop: You say “My mama don dey wait.” Somebody laughs. “Make we help your mama.” A hand closes on your phone.

recap.default: {winner} breaks for the bridge and gets exactly four steps. A foot, a shove, the tarmac. “Your pocket, oga.”
recap.coop: You break for the bridge and get exactly four steps. A foot, a shove, the tarmac. “Your pocket, oga.”

recap.default: {winner} says the vigilante men are behind. Ajala looks back. Nobody. He smiles. “You dey lie.”
recap.coop: You say the vigilante men are behind. Ajala looks back. Nobody. He smiles. “You dey lie.”

recap.default: {winner} offers ₦500. Ajala takes it, then holds out his other hand. “And the phone.”
recap.coop: You offer ₦500. Ajala takes it, then holds out his other hand. “And the phone.”

tie.recap: Nobody blinks until a car passes on the road. In its headlights the half-circle opens, and you walk on, with someone behind you.

vigilante_post.title: Vigilante Post
vigilante_post.text: A bamboo pole across the road, a hurricane lamp on a plastic chair, and three men in mismatched jackets. The oldest, Baba Sule, has a whistle round his neck and the air of owning the street. He flashes his torch at your face, then your hands. “Evening. Where you dey come from? Which house?” It is not hostile. It is an interview.
vigilante_post.stakes: They can see you home, or they can keep you here all night.

choices.label: Greet Baba Sule properly: “Baba, thank God for you people”
Pay ₦500 for the night levy and ask them to see you home

lock.reason: You don't have money left to pay with.

choices.label: Drop a big name: “I'm the Commissioner's nephew”
Give your house number, the street chairman's name, and your landlord's number

twists.text: {holder}: Baba Sule's eyes soften. “Ah, Mama Tolu sent you? Come.”
{holder}: Baba Sule rubs his finger and thumb together. Nobody says anything, but everybody thinks it.
{holder}: Baba Sule: “Which big man is that? I know the whole street.”

recap.default: {winner} greets Baba Sule like a village elder. He chuckles. “Small pikin wey get manners.” Two men stand, lamp in hand. {loser} gets a nod, not a handshake.
recap.coop: You greet Baba Sule like a village elder. He chuckles. “Small pikin wey get manners.” Two men stand, lamp in hand.

recap.default: {winner} presses ₦500 into the chair arm. One of the men whistles. “Big boy.” Two of them stand and take them home. {loser} is told to keep quiet and keep close.
recap.coop: You press ₦500 into the chair arm. One of the men whistles. “Big boy.” Two of them stand and take you home.

recap.default: {winner} says “Commissioner.” Baba Sule narrows his eyes and sighs, “Go, go,” not because he believes it but because he does not have the energy. {loser} suspects somebody will check, later.
recap.coop: You say “Commissioner.” Baba Sule narrows his eyes and sighs, “Go, go,” not because he believes it but because he does not have the energy.

recap.default: {winner} answers every question and names the street chairman. Baba Sule writes it in his notebook. “Okay. Safe journey.” {loser} stands by the pole with nothing to add.
recap.coop: You answer every question and name the street chairman. Baba Sule writes it in his notebook. “Okay. Safe journey.”

recap.default: {winner} greets him, but he is busy with a quarrel on the radio. “Wait there.” Twenty minutes later, they let them pass without a word.
recap.coop: You greet him, but he is busy with a quarrel on the radio. “Wait there.” Twenty minutes later, they let you pass without a word.

recap.default: {winner} pays ₦500. “Levy for what?” says another man. “We never ask.” The money disappears anyway, and nobody takes them home.
recap.coop: You pay ₦500. “Levy for what?” says another man. “We never ask.” The money disappears anyway, and nobody takes you home.

recap.default: {winner} says “Commissioner.” “Which one?” They check. They hold them at the post until somebody vouches. It is past midnight when they let go.
recap.coop: You say “Commissioner.” “Which one?” They check. They hold you at the post until somebody vouches. It is past midnight when they let go.

recap.default: {winner} stumbles on the chairman's name. “Hmm. Sit down. We go confirm.” It takes forty minutes.
recap.coop: You stumble on the chairman's name. “Hmm. Sit down. We go confirm.” It takes forty minutes.

tie.recap: Nobody pushes. Baba Sule looks at you a long time, lifts the pole, and lets you through.

back_lane.title: Back Lane
back_lane.text: Behind the mechanic yard the lane is the width of two goats. Wet drain on one side, a wall with broken bottles on the other. The music from the bridge is a rumour here. Somewhere a dog barks twice and stops. Every sound feels loud. A man in a singlet sits outside a gate, smoking, watching you like you are an item in a market.
back_lane.stakes: It's quiet, which is either very good or very bad.

choices.label: Greet the man at his gate: “Good night sir, I dey rush home”
Run the lane flat out and don't stop for anything
Shout, “I see you!” into a dark corner, in case somebody is there
Move slow along the wall and listen before every turn

twists.text: {holder}: There is no torch, and every shape in the lane is a person or a dog until it isn't.
{holder}: The wall is still warm from the day. You remember: left, left, then straight.

recap.default: {winner} greets the man. He grunts, then stands, fixes his singlet and walks with them to the end of the lane, because it is his lane. {loser} is told to walk in front.
recap.coop: You greet the man. He grunts, then stands, fixes his singlet and walks with you to the end of the lane, because it is his lane.

recap.default: {winner} sprints the whole lane. A drain slab shifts under one foot, but nothing else does. They come out with a sore ankle and a loud heart. {loser} comes out coughing.
recap.coop: You sprint the whole lane. A drain slab shifts under one foot, but nothing else does. You come out with a sore ankle and a loud heart.

recap.default: {winner} shouts “I see you!” Something small and quick runs off. A dog? A person? They do not wait to find out. {loser} jumps higher than anyone has ever jumped.
recap.coop: You shout “I see you!” Something small and quick runs off. A dog? A person? You do not wait to find out.

recap.default: {winner} moves slowly, wall on one side, listening. Twice, they hear something and wait it out. The lane lets them go. {loser} stays close, and quieter.
recap.coop: You move slowly, wall on one side, listening. Twice, you hear something and wait it out. The lane lets you go.

recap.default: {winner} greets the man. He thinks they are a thief and starts shouting. A door opens, a dog barks, three streets away somebody starts running.
recap.coop: You greet the man. He thinks you are a thief and starts shouting. A door opens, a dog barks, three streets away somebody starts running.

recap.default: {winner} runs. At the lane mouth, two boys step out and one grabs their arm. “Where you dey rush go?”
recap.coop: You run. At the lane mouth, two boys step out and one grabs your arm. “Where you dey rush go?”

recap.default: {winner} shouts “I see you!” Somebody answers, “Then you see me.” A shape steps out of the dark.
recap.coop: You shout “I see you!” Somebody answers, “Then you see me.” A shape steps out of the dark.

recap.default: {winner} goes so slowly that the shape in the dark has time to fall in behind them.
recap.coop: You go so slowly that the shape in the dark has time to fall in behind you.

tie.recap: The man in the singlet stares until you are past. The rest of the lane feels very long.

gate_clean.title: Your Gate: Smooth
gate_clean.text: You turn into your street and your gate is right there, lit by the neighbour's generator. Nobody is behind you. For the first time tonight, your shoulders drop. The last thing is to get inside and tell it your way.

stakes.default: Get inside first and tell the story your way.

choices.label: Call out to the gateman cheerfully so he opens up fast
Jog the last stretch and get to the gate first
Make the story bigger in your head and tell it loudly as you enter
Walk in calm, lock everything, then plan the story

gate_shaken.title: Your Gate: Late
gate_shaken.text: Your street, your gate, and your knees have not yet understood that it is over. The neighbour's generator is on, and so is the gateman's radio. You are lighter than when you left and a lot quieter. Mallam looks up from his stool. “Why you dey come this late?”

stakes.default: Get inside first, and decide how much of the story is true.
stakes.coop: Get inside and decide how much of the story is true.

choices.label: Tell Mallam something warm and short: “Just traffic, Mallam, thank you for waiting”
Hurry through the gate before he asks anything else
Tell a story big enough that nobody checks the details
Say little, lock the gate, tell it properly tomorrow

twists.text: {holder}: Your pocket is lighter than it should be. Mallam can tell from how you walk.

gate_followed.title: Your Gate: Behind You
gate_followed.text: Your gate is ahead. Behind you, slippers slap slowly on the tarmac, the way somebody walks when they don't want you to notice they're walking. Mallam's lamp is on, but he is looking at the road, not at you. If you open that gate now, whoever is behind you knows exactly where you live.
gate_followed.stakes: Don't lead them to your door.

choices.label: Turn around and greet the person like a neighbour: “Good night, I dey for here”
Walk past your gate, loop the block, and lose them
Shout for Mallam as if the whole compound is awake: “Daddy! Open!”
Walk past and wait at the neighbour's gate until the slippers pass

twists.text: {holder}: The footsteps are patient. They have been following since the bridge.

gate_robbed.title: Your Gate: Empty Pockets
gate_robbed.text: You reach your gate with your shirt pulled out of place, no phone, no money, and a ringing in your ears. Mallam looks at you a long time, then slides the bolt. “Ah ah. Wetin happen?” You still need to get inside, call your people from his phone, and decide what story to tell.
gate_robbed.stakes: You lost things tonight. Don't lose the story too.

choices.label: Borrow Mallam's phone and call home in a calm voice
Go straight to the neighbour's door and bang until somebody wakes up
Tell it bigger than it was so the whole compound stays up and worries with you
Check yourself, block the SIM, lock the compound, report in the morning

twists.text: {holder}: Your hand keeps patting the empty pocket, as if the phone will come back.

gate_escorted.title: Your Gate: With Escort
gate_escorted.text: Your own street, your own gate, a lamp on each side of you. The escorts stand off a little as Mallam peers at them through the bars. “Na them?” The men stand straight, lamps up. For the first time tonight, nobody is afraid of anybody, and nobody is leaving until you say it's fine.

stakes.default: Get inside first with your people behind you.
stakes.coop: Get inside with your people behind you.

choices.label: Thank them warmly, loudly, so Mallam hears everything
Slip each of them a small note as thanks

lock.reason: You don't have money left to pay with.

choices.label: Make it sound like you saved them tonight
Ask their names, write them down, and say you'll tell the street chairman

twists.text: {holder}: Baba Sule's men salute you, half-joking. Mallam salutes back, fully joking.

endings.win: You push your gate open first, with your phone, your money and your mouth all intact. You tell the story your way. {loser} buys suya tomorrow and tells it badly.
endings.loss: When you reach the gate, {winner} is already inside telling the story with big hands. You buy the suya.

success.default: You both get to the gate together, tired but fine. Nobody walks alone again.
success.solo: You get to the gate tired but fine. Next time, you will take a Bolt.

fail.default: You get home late and shaken, with half your things. The group chat will have the story before you sleep.
fail.solo: You get home late and shaken, with half your things. The group chat will have the story before you sleep.

epilogues.text: Since that night, you read every street before you walk it.
The boys now greet you by name whenever you pass. It is respect, or something close.
The boys have your face in their memory now. Avoid that road for a while.
You paid small money to get home. Next time you will carry a ₦200 note separately.
You got home with an empty pocket and a very long story.
Your phone went off in the dark. You charged it fully for three days after.
The big name you used got back to its owner. Enjoy that conversation.
The vigilante men now wave at you from their plastic chairs every evening.
You will be buying a new phone this month.
The keke rider now saves your number. Last trip, any time.
